newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia deports 19 Vietnamese amid U.N. protests.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia deports 19 Vietnamese amid U.N. protests.

text.p: Cambodia on Thursday deported 19 anti-Hanoi activists to Vietnam, drawing an angry response from the United Nations which said the move violated international rights conventions.

"We are of course disappointed that despite our intervention and the government knowing our position, these people were taken to Vietnam," Peter Van der Vaat, Cambodia mission chief for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), told Reuters.
"We told the government, if they are deported, that is at odds with the 1951 (Geneva) Convention on refugees," he said, adding that some of the political activists may face danger in Vietnam.

Interior Ministry officials said at a press conference that the activists were among 28 members of the U.S.-based anti-Hanoi People's Action Party who were detained last week for allegedly seeking to enter Thailand illegally.
The 19 activists, including three women and a monk, would be immediately deported to the Vietnamese border for illegally attempting to enter Thailand, the officials said.
In addition, one U.S. citizen among the group had overstayed his visa and would be deported to the United States, they said.
Interior Ministry spokesman Heng Hak said the government would "re-educate" and eventually release the remaining eight, who had Cambodian identity papers.
Heng Hak said the government was following international immigration law, adding, "We have informed the Vietnamese embassy, but we don't know if they will be detained in Vietnam."
The sombre-looking activists were loaded onto a truck at the close of the press conference in the capital.
As he was led to a military truck, Vietnamese-American Charly Ly, 31, said, "I don't have any power. I have no choice," but added, "We will fight to the end."
Van der Vaat said that after meeting the detainees on Wednesday, the UNHCR submitted a letter to Police Chief Hok Lundi asking the government to reconsider the deportation plan.
An official from the U.N. Centre for Human Rights said his agency also met the detainees and was concerned for their safety.
Nam Nguyen, a representative of the People's Action Party contacted by telephone in Bangkok, said she was worried about the fate of the 19 activists.
"You go back to the tiger's cage, and you don't know what will happen to your safety," she said.
